Drywall repair in Halton

A hole, an old patch, or a visible seam can leave a room feeling unfinished. Define the repair and the finish together, so everyone knows where patching ends and decorating begins.

Jobs to discuss

Holes & local damage

Small impact damage, old fixing holes, and damaged areas to assess for a patch or replacement section.

Seams & old patches

Visible joints, rough repairs, and uneven areas to discuss before repainting.

Taping & finishing

Finishing work on drywall, including the extent of the surface preparation and the intended painted finish.

Agree on the finished surface

A patch is only one part of the brief. Record whether the job stops at a surface ready for primer or also includes priming and painting. A local touch-up and repainting a whole wall are different scopes.

  • How large is the damaged area, and is it on a wall or ceiling?
  • Is the surface flat, textured, or covered with another finish?
  • Has the damage returned after a previous repair?
  • Who is responsible for primer, paint, and the surrounding finish?

Before settling the scope

Describe staining, dampness, or a crack that keeps returning before requesting a cosmetic patch. The cause and any concealed damage need to be assessed before the repair scope is settled. Basement framing and changes to a layout are a separate conversation.

YOUR PROJECT BRIEF

What to include

  • Your city, the room, and whether the area is on a wall or ceiling.
  • An approximate size, plus close-up and wider photographs ready to discuss.
  • What caused the damage, if known, and the finish you want afterward.

For example

There is a roughly 20 cm hole in the hallway wall from moving furniture. The wall has a flat painted finish. Please separate patching and preparation from repainting the wall.

Planning questions

Is painting included in a drywall repair?

It needs to be stated in the scope. Ask for patching, preparation, primer, and painting to be identified so you can compare proposals on the same basis.

Can a small patch be made invisible?

Set expectations after looking at the existing texture, coating, and lighting. Do not assume a local repair and paint touch-up will match the entire surface.

What if the same crack has been repaired before?

Include that history, when the crack returned, and any changes nearby. Ask what needs investigating before another finish repair is proposed.
